newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: Uzbekistan to hold 17.29 bln yen airport tender.
newsitem.headline: Uzbekistan to hold 17.29 bln yen airport tender.

text.p: The Uzbek national airline has announced an international 17.288 billion yen tender to modernise airports in the cities of Samarkand, Bukhara and Urgench, tender coordinator Khairulla Abdullayev said.
The tender, initiated by national carrier Uzbekiston Khavo Yullari, is open for all countries and starts on September 20, Abdullayev said.
Most of the value of the tender is covered by a loan from Japan's Overseas Economic Cooperation Fund (OECF).

"In line with the credit agreement between the Uzbek government and the OECF, the Japanese partner allots 15.526 billion yen, the remaining 1.762 billion being contributed in the national sum currency by the air company," he said.

A source at the Japanese embassy in Tashkent told Reuters that the credit has already been approved by the Japanese government. The loan is being granted for 30 years at 2.7 percent annual with a grace period of 10 years.
Abdullayev said the project includes the modernisation of runways, landing systems, lighting and terminals as the first stage.
The second stage, for which another tender will be announced, will include upgrading taxiways and air traffic control facilities.
Bids will be accepted until November 18. The first stage of the reconstruction is due to start in January to be over by September next year, Abdullayev said.

The OECF loan for the tender is the third granted by the Fund to Uzbekistan. In June 1995 it allotted a 12.7 billion yen loan for the development of telecommunications. Another 6.1 billion yen were earmarked in June this year to build a railway wagon-repair plant in Tashkent.
